items.review_rationale: Checked the specified quotient presentation of a relative complete-intersection map, with its finite polynomial generators and relations and the dimension condition on every nonempty scheme fibre rather than only global Krull dimension.

references.context: Multivariable polynomial R-algebra in finitely many indeterminates
Commutative ring quotient by the finitely generated ideal of relations f_i

references.phrase: Krull dimension of each nonempty fibre
dimension n−c for all nonempty fibres
references.disposition: This is the stipulated relative expected-dimension condition; zero fibres are excluded and it is not merely the absolute dimension of Spec(S).

items.review_rationale: Reviewed all three syntomic conditions with the correct unital ring-map convention: flatness, finite presentation and local-complete-intersection algebra structure after residue-field base change at every prime.

references.phrase: local complete intersection algebra over κ(p)
base change S⊗_R κ(p) of the ring map

references.context: For p∈Spec(R), fraction field of local residue ring R_p/pR_p; not an arbitrary extension field

references.phrase: tensor-product algebra structure on S⊗_R κ(p)
references.context: Induced commutative κ(p)-algebra multiplication on the module tensor product under base change

references.disposition: The fibre condition is imposed at every prime; there is no claim that flatness or local complete intersection alone suffices.

items.review_rationale: Read the finite-union normal form for constructible subsets of an arbitrary affine prime spectrum, separately identifying distinguished opens and finite-equation closed loci without importing a Noetherian hypothesis.

references.phrase: Zariski topology on the affine spectrum

references.context: Subset of prime ideals not containing f in R, for a commutative ring R
Subset of prime ideals of R containing every specified relation g_i, equivalently V of the generated ideal

references.disposition: Finite union and intersection are set operations; the displayed constructible normal form assumes no Noetherian condition.

items.review_rationale: Read the defining field and finite-underlying-set clauses, then distinguished the asserted prime-power cardinality classification as a mathematical consequence rather than an extra independent axiom.

references.context: Number theory: positive integer p>1 with no positive divisors except 1 and p, not a prime ideal

references.disposition: Prime-power size is a theorem about finite fields, not an additional defining condition or a source of arbitrary finite cardinalities.
